tagline: From the cemetery into the ground of an early victory.
intro: From Kentucky 80 at Nancy, the byway follows KY 235 and Old Mill Springs Battlefield Road for 10.36 miles, to the end of the road at the Ferry Landing, Tour Stop 8. On this largely rural ground, Union forces under George H. Thomas beat the Confederates on January 19, 1862.

Felix Zollicoffer, conspicuous in a white raincoat, approached the Union 4th Kentucky believing they were his own men, and was shot. Mill Springs, the town that named the battle, lies across Lake Cumberland, a separate drive by Highways 90 and 1275.

moments.title: Mill Springs National Cemetery
moments.text: Begun as the battlefield cemetery, with the fallen buried in large trenches, it later took in remains from other battlefield cemeteries in the region, and the battlefield museum stands next door.

moments.title: Mill Springs battlefield
moments.text: A marked stump is what lightning left of the Zollie Tree, the tree attributed as the place where Zollicoffer fell.

moments.title: Mill Springs Mill
moments.text: Across the lake stands an 1877 mill with a 40-foot wheel, below springs Daniel Boone reportedly found, and on seasonal weekends it grinds corn for visitors.
